one_line: A shared contract and canvas workspace where humans and agents co-edit with freshness checks and human commits.
what_it_does: Provides real-time shared contract editing and structured visual-canvas collaboration with revision receipts, stale-mutation rejection, inline approval, and reviewed restores.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to the product's shared-state contract: agents read browser-held receipts, receive intervening changes, and cannot silently overwrite fresher human or agent work.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies opaque browser read receipts and server rejection of stale mutations.
The stated workflow shares live contract/canvas state and revision history between humans and agents.
Frame sheets show a populated collaborative visual workspace across multiple states.
execution_rationale: The packet describes two coherent workspaces and the frame sheets show a substantial, populated application rather than a static landing page; exact end-to-end commit behavior is not readable in the contact sheets.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion frame sheets show a structured canvas/workspace with changing states.
Description names local drafts, inline approval, immutable revisions, restores, and hydration handling.
Demo is marked alive.
impact_rationale: Concurrent human-agent editing is a real collaboration problem, and protecting local work and review authority addresses a concrete failure mode for teams using agents.
impact_evidence: Specific audience is teams co-editing contracts and visual artifacts.
Description identifies stale edits and silent overwrites as the motivating problem.
Visible workspace presents a usable collaboration surface.
creativity_rationale: The combination of browser-held freshness receipts, agent collaboration, and human commit controls is an ambitious and memorable interaction model for shared documents and canvases.
creativity_evidence: One concept spans structured contract editing and Excalidraw collaboration.
Freshness protocol hides revision numbers from agents while enforcing review-and-retry.
Frame sheets show a distinctive visual collaborative workspace.
usability_note: The described human draft/commit and revision surfaces are promising, though small frames do not establish ease of use.
red_flags: Exact agent invocation and final commit outcome are not legible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Freshness-aware shared state with human commit authority.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific collaboration design with substantial visible product evidence.

leverage_rationale: Structured tools let an agent compare records, constraints, citations, and draft state reliably; the owner-only approval boundary is part of the tool and application contract.

one_line: A live-page audit and repair layer where agents propose bounded fixes and humans approve each DOM change.
what_it_does: Scans accessibility, SEO, and performance issues, highlights live elements, proposes evidence-backed fixes, pauses for human approval, rescans, supports revert, and exports patches.
leverage_rationale: The live DOM, unresolved approval call, evidence-backed patch, rescan, and revert loop is substantially more reliable and shared-state-aware than an agent inferring a page through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies nine imperative tools spanning scan, highlight, propose, apply, revert, and export.
apply_fix remains unresolved until a human clicks Approve or Skip.
Agent and human inspect the same live element and post-approval rescan the page.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a complete bounded workflow and reports a concrete fixture progression from 54 to 100 with 23 approved changes; frame sheets and packaging show a results-oriented audit interface.
execution_evidence: Description reports 23 issues, pack scores, 23 approved changes, and post-fix 100 scores.
Frame sheets show progression from landing presentation into populated issue/result screens.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows issue checklist/status presentation.
impact_rationale: Web accessibility, SEO, and performance defects are concrete problems for site owners, and a human-gated repair loop directly addresses diagnosis, safe correction, and verification.
impact_evidence: Three rule packs target recognizable website quality problems.
Tool refuses to invent human-facing content and requests agent-authored input where needed.
Reported fixture outcome is a complete verified score improvement.
creativity_rationale: Keeping an agent physically and procedurally on the live page while suspending mutation until human approval is an original, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Human approval is implemented as a pending tool call rather than a post-hoc confirmation.
Each patch carries evidence and authoredBy metadata.
Revert and export extend the concept beyond a one-shot audit.
usability_note: Visible issue lists, highlights, approval sheet, rescans, and revert form a clear operational loop.
red_flags: Exact tool invocation text is not readable in the frame sheets, though the described outcomes are specific.
standouts: Exceptionally strong live-DOM, approval-gated, evidence-and-rescan workflow.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP leverage and complete evidence-backed workflow.

creativity_rationale: Animated diffs are a useful creative extension of code-image tools, though the category and core concept are an incremental synthesis rather than wholly unprecedented.

Styling and export are integrated into the concept.
Hand-built rendering pipeline handles DOM animation capture.
